overall: Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by discussing collective bargaining matters in a contract-negotiations executive session; the no-second and announcement-timing complaints were not violations.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the committee entered executive session after its November 22, 2011 meeting without announcing a reason for doing so.
allegations.key_passage: while the Committee announced a valid reason for entering into executive session, the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by discussing matters in executive session that were not appropriate given the stated purpose

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the motion to enter executive session was not properly seconded.
allegations.key_passage: there is no requirement in the Open Meeting Law that a motion to enter executive session be seconded, only that the ensuing vote be taken by roll call

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the chair announced the executive session purpose at the start of the meeting rather than immediately before entering executive session.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law is silent in regards to when during a meeting the chair must state the executive session purpose, therefore we do not find that the Committee violated the law by making its executive session announcement at the beginning of the meeting

remedy: We order immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and offer this letter as future guidance.
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and offer this letter as future guidance.
